samples.summary: The case-insensitive `data:` detection fix (`/^data:/i`) has no test — no case exercises an uppercase `DATA:` src with `inlineImages` off
samples.evidence: `imageInline` changed `image.src.startsWith('data:')` to `/^data:/i.test(image.src)`, and the inline comment states this was a real bug ("Spelled `DATA:` this test used to answer `false`, so a data URL was emitted inline with `inlineImages` off — the one thing this branch exists to prevent"). Every test in packages/docs/test/serialize/markdown.test.ts that touches the data-URI branch uses lowercase `data:` (lines 343-378, 650-654, 705-710). Reverting the `/i` would not fail any test: `SAFE_IMAGE_DATA_URI` is already `/i`, so `DATA:image/png;base64,AAAA` with `inlineImages:false` would be emitted verbatim and nothing asserts otherwise.

samples.summary: `sectPrLengthPx`'s `allowZero` distinction is untested — no test asserts that a `<w:pgMar>` value of `0` survives as a 0 margin
samples.evidence: `allowZero` exists solely to separate "a page dimension of 0 is broken" from "a margin of 0 is a legitimate edge-to-edge layout". The new tests in packages/docs/test/import/docx-parser.test.ts cover non-numeric and negative margins and non-numeric/negative/zero/empty page sizes, but never `<w:pgMar w:top="0"/>`. Because every other new docx case is also caught downstream by `resolvePageSetup` (NaN/negative/zero all fall back there), the entire new helper could be deleted and all four new docx assertions would still pass; the one case that would actually distinguish it (margin 0 kept as 0 rather than defaulted to 96) is the one not written. A regression here silently changes imported document margins.

samples.summary: `fitMargins`' documented proportional shrink is not tested — the tests only assert the content box is `> 0`, which a reset-to-default would also satisfy
samples.evidence: `fitMargins` documents "Proportional rather than reset-to-default so a document whose margins are merely too large for its page keeps the ratio its author chose." The covering tests (packages/docs/test/model/types.test.ts, 'leaves a positive content box when margins would close it', and the docx 'leaves a positive content box when the margins swallow the page') assert only `> 0` on the resulting content box, and use symmetric margins (5000/5000, 20000/20000) where a ratio cannot be observed. Replacing the proportional scale with `return [defaultNear, defaultFar]` or `[0, 0]` would pass every assertion.

samples.summary: The refactored ruler margin-drag write path (`ruler.onMarginChange` → `writePageSetup`, which now throws) has no test
samples.evidence: The handler at editor.ts:2073 was rewritten to route through `writePageSetup`, which calls `assertUsablePageSetup` and can now throw a `RangeError` from inside a drag callback where it previously could not. `packages/docs/test/view/ruler.test.ts` contains no occurrence of 'margin', 'snapshot' or 'setPageSetup' (grep returned 0 matches), and the new editor-page-setup tests drive only `EditorAPI.setPageSetup`. Nothing exercises the ruler callback, so a throw escaping into the drag handler — or the reordered snapshot (now taken after the assert) breaking undo for a ruler drag — would ship unnoticed.

samples.summary: No test asserts that a page-setup write actually invalidates the layout / repaginates
samples.evidence: `writePageSetup` is documented as "drop the cached layout so `paginateLayout` runs against the new paper size / margins, repaint". packages/docs/test/view/editor-page-setup.test.ts asserts only the stored/read-back setup, the undo step and aliasing. If `invalidateLayout()` were removed, every assertion in that file would still pass while the user saw stale pagination after changing paper size — a visible defect.
searchedFor: grep `getPageCount|pageCount` in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts (no observable API found)

samples.evidence: The `EditorAPI.pasteFormat` wrapper added at editor.ts calls `notifyStyleApplied()` when the paste applied, so the toolbar pickers re-read their summaries. Neither packages/docs/test/view/editor-format-painter.test.ts nor the frontend toggle test observes any cursor-move/style-applied notification after a paste; the frontend test stubs `onCursorMove` as `vi.fn(() => () => {})` and never asserts it fires. Dropping the notify call would leave the toolbar showing stale formatting after a paint, with no failing test.

samples.summary: The non-CR/LF line separators in `LINE_SEPARATORS` (U+0085, U+2028, U+2029) are untested
`resolvePageSetup`'s orientation normalization (anything not `'landscape'` becomes `'portrait'`) is untested for a garbage stored value
samples.evidence: The new line `resolved.orientation === 'landscape' ? 'landscape' : 'portrait'` coerces an arbitrary stored orientation, which is exactly the CRDT-write case the doc comment cites. The new tests in packages/docs/test/model/types.test.ts only pass valid `'portrait'`/`'landscape'`; no case passes e.g. `'sideways'` or `undefined` to check the coercion.

samples.summary: Assertion `expect(resolved.paperSize.height).toBe(1056)` is vacuous — 1056 is also the default height, so it holds whether or not height was preserved
samples.evidence: In the it.each 'falls back to the default paper width for %s', the fixture sets `height: 1056`, which equals `DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP.paperSize.height`. The assertion is intended to show that only the bad width falls back, but it passes identically if height were also replaced by the default. Using a non-default height (e.g. 1000) would make it meaningful.
